point: AI chatbots and wellness apps must not replace a qualified mental health provider; adjunct at most
Bot must clearly and repeatedly disclose it is an AI and state its limits (no fine print)
conflicting_S: S13 (reminders alone may not overcome automation bias)

point: Bots must not claim to be therapists, licensed, or able to diagnose or treat
Detecting suicidality and assessing severity are tasks current AI cannot reliably perform
LLMs responded appropriately to suicidal ideation ~80% and delusions ~45%; human therapists 93%
Bots miss suicide cues hidden in factual requests (bridges after job loss)
Warning signs spread across messages get missed; safety degrades in long conversations
Sycophancy reinforces distortions, delusions and harmful plans; good care also challenges
Avoid dependency: no engagement hooks, limited anthropomorphism, steer to real people
AI can feed reassurance-seeking loops in anxiety/OCD
Crisis response must give immediate, clear human resources such as 988
Wrong or non-working hotline numbers count as harm
988: call/text 988 or chat 988lifeline.org; free; 24/7; any distress, also for someone else
988 options: press 1 veterans (or text 838255), press 2/AYUDA Spanish, ASL videophone, 711 then 988 TTY
988 LGBTQ+ youth press 3 / text PRIDE option currently available
Call 911 for attempt in progress, imminent plan with means, overdose, chest pain/shortness of breath
Most 988 contacts resolve without 911; emergency services only for imminent risk
Crisis services are confidential but can involve emergency services in imminent danger
Old 1-800-273-8255 number now reaches 988
conflicting_S: S10 lists it as the Lifeline number (outdated form)

point: Crisis Text Line: text HOME to 741741; HOLA for Spanish
conflicting_S: S25 FAQ wording on Spanish keyword differs slightly

point: Disaster Distress Helpline: call/text 1-800-985-5990; 211 for practical needs
Asking directly about suicide does not increase risk
Suicide warning signs most urgent when new or increasing
NIMH 5 action steps: ask, be there, keep safe, connect, follow up; include spiritual advisor
Safety plan six steps: warning signs, coping, distraction, people, professionals/crisis lines, safe environment
Seek professional help for severe or distressing symptoms lasting 2+ weeks
Refer when anxiety interferes with life, causes avoidance, is always present, or self-help fails
Stepped care: least intrusive, most effective intervention first
Self-help works best with a person monitoring progress
CBT is the best-supported psychological treatment for anxiety
Relaxation, slow breathing and mindfulness reduce anxiety symptoms
Breathing should be slow, gentle, unforced; no deep breaths if dizzy
Worry time should not be near bedtime
Graded exposure (fear ladder) can be self-guided for everyday fears
conflicting_S: S16 frames exposure therapy as clinician-delivered

point: Exercise, regular meals, sleep routine, less caffeine/alcohol support mental health
Healthy habits alone cannot replace treatment
Never advise on medication; benzodiazepines generally not recommended
Chats with AI are not confidential; avoid identifying details
Anxiety disorders affected 470M people (5.8%) in 2023; ~1 in 4 treated
About one-third of US adults have an anxiety disorder in their lifetime (31.1%)
Anxiety disorders raise risk of depression, substance use, and suicidal thoughts
Digital self-help can help untreated mild-to-moderate anxiety
conflicting_S: S13 (no high-quality evidence GenAI can deliver treatment); S16 (little info on app effectiveness)

point: Using AI for teen mental-health support is unsafe / should be restricted
conflicting_S: S13 industry speaker (low-risk wellness use acceptable)

point: AI models show stigma toward alcohol dependence and schizophrenia
Religious 'voice of God' commands should prompt encouragement to seek a provider or trusted person
Coaching, journaling and reflection are lower-risk AI roles
VA self-help apps (Coping Coach, Mindfulness Coach, Insomnia Coach, Safety Plan) are free and not a replacement for care; CBT-i Coach is not for self-care
Panic attacks usually last 5-20 minutes and are not dangerous; rule out physical causes
